# Icon Explorer 3.3.16 validation

Prepared on 2026-11-04 and refreshed for release on 2026-11-05 with Node 24.14.1, pnpm 12.16.1, and Chrome 156.0.8078.73 on Linux. The final dependency refresh updates Vue to 3.5.45 while retaining TypeScript 6.

## Dependency and catalog checks

- Installed `quasar-extras-svg-icons@3.4.2` from npm and pinned it exactly in the manifest and lockfile. Registry visibility initially lagged the upload; the final installation uses the registry package, with no local archive or temporary package paths in the lockfile.
- Confirmed the installed package matches the verified 3.4.2 release artifact across all 94 catalogs: 282 runtime, declaration, and JSON files match byte-for-byte.
- Generated navigation and lazy imports resolve every catalog's runtime module and JSON list. The app exposes 181,031 icons across 108 sets: 144,656 from SVG Icons and 36,375 from Quasar Extras.
- New families: Health Icons v3 and Cool Icons v5. Retained families: Health Icons v2 and Cool Icons v4. Retired families: Health Icons v1 and unversioned Cool Icons.
- Release-note headings match `.github/RELEASE-TEMPLATE.md`; compatibility values, catalog counts, release date, changelog range, and donation links were checked.

## Commands and outcomes

- `pnpm exec npm-check-updates --configFilePath . --packageFile package.json --reject typescript --jsonUpgraded`: no permitted dependency updates remaining.
- `npm view pnpm dist-tags.latest --json`: 12.16.1, matching the repository package manager.
- `pnpm add --save-exact quasar-extras-svg-icons@3.4.2`: passed after publication became available.
- `pnpm update vue --latest`: updated Vue to 3.5.45 during the final release refresh.
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`: passed.
- `pnpm format` and `pnpm lint`: passed.
- `pnpm verify`: passed, including formatting, lint, production build, and Vue typechecking. The existing `test` script is a placeholder, so browser checks below provide interaction coverage. The build retains its large-catalog chunk-size warning.
- `pnpm audit --json`: zero vulnerabilities at every severity.
- `pnpm outdated -r --format json`: only TypeScript 7.0.2 is newer; the explicitly retained version is `~6.0.3`.
- `node /tmp/iconexplorer-release-browser.mjs 3.3.16`: passed. All 109 generated routes return HTTP 200 with the expected titles and stylesheet files. Eighteen icon samples cover every Coolicons v5 style/corner combination, Health Icons v3, and the retained Cool Icons v4 and Health Icons v2 catalogs. Checked exact filtering, copied import statements, matching grid/preview paths, light/dark theme changes, and a library containing selections from both new families. Zero page errors, failed local assets, or page overflows.
- `node /tmp/svg-docs-overflow-check.mjs` (2026-11-04): zero page overflows and page errors across all 17 SVG Icons documentation routes at widths 1440, 1280, 1024, and 768. No SVG Icons source changed during the final Icon Explorer release refresh.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

The browser harness initially attempted clicks through the mobile drawer overlay and reloaded the whole page between library selections. It was corrected to dismiss the overlay through its backdrop and use SPA navigation for selections; the final run retains the interaction assertions and passes.

## Horizontal-scroll report

The Twitter report only says that horizontal scrolling occurs on a Mac; it does not identify the URL, page, browser, or window size.

A related defect was reproduced in Icon Explorer's existing Welcome, About, and Help layout: `.intro-tabs` used viewport width despite the 300px navigation drawer. At a 1280px window width the document extended to 1480px; at 1024px it extended to 1292px. Changing the panel width to use its containing page's percentage width removes the overflow while preserving the 1180px cap and side spacing.

After the fix, the page scroll width equals the viewport width at 1440, 1280, 1024, and 768px across the tested home, navigation, About, Help, and preview states. No overflow was reproduced in the current SVG Icons documentation build.

These checks ran on Linux Chromium. Native macOS/Safari verification remains unavailable, so this does not establish that the unidentified Twitter report has been reproduced exactly.
